holidays.name: Mean Girls Day
holidays.description: Fans of the 2004 cult classic wear pink, quote the movie endlessly, and celebrate the date Aaron Samuels asks Cady Heron what day it is. Expect fetch references, Burn Book jokes, and plenty of people declaring that on Wednesdays we wear pink.
holidays.origin: In the film, Aaron asks Cady what the date is and she replies, 'October third.' The line became an internet meme, and the studio, cast, and fans began celebrating the date every year.
holidays.funFact: The film is based on Rosalind Wiseman's self-help book 'Queen Bees and Wannabes,' and Tina Fey wrote the screenplay, which was inspired by that nonfiction parenting guide.

holidays.name: National Boyfriend Day
holidays.description: A day for people to show appreciation for their boyfriends with gifts, dinners, cheesy social media posts, and heartfelt gestures. It is also an excuse to finally give him credit for always carrying your jacket.
holidays.origin: This unofficial observance emerged from social media in the 2010s and is celebrated on October 3, with National Girlfriend Day falling in August. Its origins are informal rather than tied to a specific founder.
holidays.funFact: The date often trends online each year, even though no official organization or government recognizes it.

holidays.name: National Techies Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the people who keep our computers, phones, and Wi-Fi alive, from IT help desk heroes to software developers. It is the perfect day to finally say thank you instead of just asking whether they tried turning it off and on again.
holidays.origin: National Techies Day was created in 2014 by Lisa Silverman to recognize people in the tech industry and to inspire young people to explore careers in technology.
holidays.funFact: The phrase 'turn it off and on again' has become so iconic in tech support culture that it inspired a famous running gag in the British sitcom 'The IT Crowd.'

holidays.name: National Caramel Custard Day
holidays.description: A day to enjoy the silky, wobbly dessert of caramel custard, also known as flan or crème caramel. Dessert lovers celebrate by serving a jiggling dome with glossy caramel sauce dripping down the sides.
holidays.origin: This is a food holiday observed on October 3 by dessert fans. Its exact founder is unclear, but the dessert itself has ancient roots, with versions appearing in Roman, Spanish, and French cuisine.
holidays.funFact: The caramel is made first and poured into the bottom of the mold, so when the custard is flipped over, the caramel ends up on top as a natural sauce.

holidays.name: National Virtual Working Day
holidays.description: A holiday recognizing the joys of working remotely, from pajama pants beneath a business shirt to meetings where someone is always on mute. It encourages people to appreciate flexible work arrangements.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance that grew out of the rise of telecommuting and digital workplaces, becoming more popular as remote work expanded.
holidays.funFact: Surveys of remote workers often find that many have joined video calls wearing a professional top and casual bottoms, making the 'business on top, pajamas on the bottom' look a modern workplace classic.
